propositions: When two bundle objects exist for the same S3 ref, git-remote-s3's helper rejects all push operations and clone/fetch fail with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', rendering the store unclonable and preventing writes until the conflict is resolved.

Upstream's git-remote-s3 Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles requires interactive input (blocking on EOF) and discards the non-chosen bundle head, causing permanent data loss of events unique to the discarded head — unacceptable for an append-only ticket event log.

The doctor must perform a lossless 2-parent merge of all divergent bundle heads (never octopus, never discard), reusing rebar's existing merge semantics from sync._union_merge, with shared mutable files (.bridge_state/*) resolved via merge=ours and UUID-named event dirs never colliding.

The heal must acquire the helper's per-ref conditional-put lock (S3Remote.acquire_lock/release_lock with TTL/steal), write the merged tip as a new bundle before deleting any original, and maintain crash-safety such that at least one bundle carrying the full merged history is always present remotely.

The doctor must be invoked from push.py's retry loop exactly once (healed_once guard) when the multi-bundle signature is detected, run under rebar's write_lock to serialize against local committers, and reuse git-remote-s3's own S3Remote/.s3 client without adding direct boto3 or S3 credential dependencies to core rebar.
